panels.title: 1. Publisher/consumer scrape health
panels.description: Answers: is Prometheus actually reaching each process? Inspect next: if red, check the process is running and its /metrics port, before trusting any other panel on this dashboard -- every other panel's data is only as fresh as this.

panels.title: 2. Command and consumer attempt rates by outcome
panels.description: Answers: is work actually progressing, and in what mix of outcomes? Inspect next: a sudden shift toward 'rejected'/'conflict'/'buffered' without a matching rise in 'committed'/'applied' suggests a fencing or ordering problem, not normal operation.

panels.title: 3. Publish failures/retries
panels.description: Answers: is the publisher successfully reaching NATS? Inspect next: a sustained non-zero 'failed' rate alongside a flat 'published' rate means NATS or the publisher's network path is the actual problem, not the application logic.

panels.title: 4. Outbox backlog and oldest-event age
panels.description: Answers: is the publisher keeping up with the outbox, and for how long has the oldest row been waiting? Inspect next: a rising age with a flat/low count means one specific row is stuck (query outbox_events directly), not a volume problem. ONLY the current leader publisher exposes this -- see docs/METRICS.md.

panels.title: 5. Pending gaps and affected tasks
panels.description: Answers: how many events are durably buffered waiting on a missing predecessor, and how many distinct tasks does that affect? Inspect next: query task_consumer_state WHERE gap_detected=1 for the affected task IDs -- this panel only shows counts, never IDs (see docs/METRICS.md label discipline).

panels.title: 6. Deduplication and identity conflicts
panels.description: Answers: how often is redelivery happening, and is any of it a genuine identity conflict (a protocol-violation tripwire) rather than an ordinary duplicate? Inspect next: any non-zero 'conflict' rate warrants investigating consumer_event_conflicts directly -- it should not happen if the publisher is correct.

panels.title: 7. Processing duration distributions (p50/p95)
panels.description: Answers: how long does command processing and consumer processing actually take? Inspect next: these are quantiles over whatever traffic this dev environment has actually seen -- do NOT read a p95 here as a measured production performance characteristic (see CLAUDE.md 'never state a performance number that was not actually measured' and docs/METRICS.md).

panels.title: 8. Quarantine state
panels.description: Answers: how many messages are durably dead-lettered, and what's driving new ones? Inspect next: `npm run quarantine:inspect` for the actual messages -- this panel shows counts/rates only, never payload content (see docs/OBSERVABILITY.md).

panels.title: 9. Durable-gauge refresh freshness
panels.description: Answers: can the outbox/gap/quarantine gauges above be trusted as current, or are they stale? Inspect next: if this rises above ~30s (RelaylabDurableGaugeRefreshStale's threshold) for any group, treat every gauge in panels 4/5/8 for that group as STALE, not healthy -- check that process's own logs for the refresh failure.
